name: Tacoma Narrows
hint: Only a 19 m/s breeze today - but it pulses, lifting and dropping the deck in a rhythm that matches a slender suspension deck. Hung on plain vertical hangers, the deck gallops until it tears itself apart. Stiffen it: diagonal hangers between cable and deck (or a truss above it) make it bounce faster than the wind pushes.

history.name: Tacoma Narrows
history.type: Suspension with a shallow plate-girder deck
facts: Its deck girders were only 2.4 m deep, so it rippled even in light winds - drivers nicknamed it "Galloping Gertie".
Four months after opening, a steady 64 km/h wind set off self-exciting aeroelastic flutter that twisted the deck apart.
The only death was Tubby, a cocker spaniel left in a car on the bridge. The collapse was filmed and is studied by engineers to this day.
history.why: Its failure founded bridge aerodynamics: every long-span bridge since has been tested against wind. A stiffer replacement opened in 1950.
history.note: The wind sweeps through the rhythm of a plain suspension deck: hang yours on vertical hangers alone and watch it gallop.
